title.en: Define a multivibrator and its three types
Calculate its frequency and duty cycle

say.en: Couple two transistor switches so that when one turns on it turns the other off. Depending on the coupling, the pair blinks on its own, gives one pulse, or remembers a bit. In this lesson: Define a multivibrator and its three types.
Explain the transistor astable multivibrator.
Calculate its frequency and duty cycle.

body.en: A multivibrator is a two-stage amplifier with 100% positive feedback, in which the output of each stage drives the other. Each transistor works as a switch, either saturated (ON) or cut off (OFF), so the output is a rectangular wave. An *astable* multivibrator has no stable state: it switches by itself and is a free-running square-wave generator (clock). A monostable has one stable and one quasi-stable state: a trigger flips it for a fixed time, so it is a one-shot pulse generator or timer. A bistable has two stable states and changes only when triggered: it is a flip-flop, used as a memory element and in counters.

points.en: *Monostable*: 1 stable state, one pulse per trigger

narration.en: Multivibrators use full positive feedback between two switching stages. Astable has no stable state, monostable has one, and bistable has two.

body.en: In the *astable* circuit, the collector of Q1 is coupled to the base of Q2 through C1, and the collector of Q2 to the base of Q1 through C2; base resistors R1, R2 return to VCC. When Q1 switches on, its collector falls and C1 drives the base of Q2 negative, cutting Q2 off. C1 then charges through R2 until Q2 turns on again, which in turn cuts Q1 off through C2. Each half-period is about $0.69RC$ of the base resistor and capacitor concerned, so $T = 0.69(R_1C_1 + R_2C_2)$; for a symmetric circuit $T = 1.38RC$. The monostable replaces one capacitor coupling with a resistor; the bistable uses resistor coupling on both sides.

problem.en: A symmetric transistor astable has R1 = R2 = 10 kΩ and C1 = C2 = 0.1 µF. Find its period and frequency.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A symmetric transistor astable has R1 = R2 = 10 kΩ and C1 = C2 = 0.1 µF. Find its period and frequency.

say.en: Let us work this out together. A symmetric transistor astable has R1 equals R2 equals 10 k ohms and C1 equals C2 equals 0.1 microfarads. Find its period and frequency.
Each half-period equals 0.69 times 10 to the power 4 times 10 to the power minus 7 equals 0.69 milliseconds.
T equals 2 times 0.69 equals 1.38 milliseconds.
f equals 1 over 1.38 milliseconds equals 724.6 hertz.
So the answer is T equals 1.38 milliseconds, f is approximately 725 hertz.

problem.en: An astable has R1 = 10 kΩ, C1 = 0.1 µF, R2 = 20 kΩ and C2 = 0.1 µF. Find the frequency and the duty cycle (T1/T).

narration.en: Let us work this out together. An astable has R1 = 10 kΩ, C1 = 0.1 µF, R2 = 20 kΩ and C2 = 0.1 µF. Find the frequency and the duty cycle (T1/T).

say.en: Let us work this out together. An astable has R1 equals 10 k ohms, C1 equals 0.1 microfarads, R2 equals 20 k ohms and C2 equals 0.1 microfarads. Find the frequency and the duty cycle (T1/T).
T1 equals 0.69 times 10 to the power 4 times 10 to the power minus 7 equals 0.69 milliseconds; T2 equals 0.69 times 2 times 10 to the power 4 times 10 to the power minus 7 equals 1.38 milliseconds.
T equals 2.07 milliseconds, so f equals 483 hertz.
Duty cycle equals 0.69 over 2.07 equals 33.3 percent.
So the answer is f is approximately 483 hertz; duty cycle 33.3 percent.
